name: Dialogue-First Codex Workbench ("Salon de discussion") — UX-first chat surface over codex app-server, with the raw terminal demoted to an escape hatch
coreIdea: Start from the OpenCode UX contract — a scrollable message feed of typed cards (markdown assistant text, collapsible reasoning, command-execution cards with live output, per-file diff cards, approval prompts), a multiline composer with slash commands and prompt history, and a unified session sidebar — and work backwards to the smallest backend delta that can feed it. The verdict from the research is unambiguous: the PTY byte stream can never feed this UX (raw ANSI TUI redraws), but the codebase already contains every seam needed. So the design is a two-track engine behind ONE chat UI: (Track A, ships first, near-zero backend) render historical transcripts from the rollout JSONL that discussions.rs already knows how to find, and drive live sessions through the existing sendLine()/write_terminal bridge; (Track B, the real engine) a thin Rust JSON-RPC pump around `codex app-server --stdio` (the officially documented integration surface, already prototyped in settings.rs::read_server_rate_limits) that forwards item-lifecycle notifications verbatim to the frontend as a single new event, where a vanilla-TS chat store reduces them into cards. No framework migration: the chat root is a persistent DOM subtree mounted OUTSIDE the render() innerHTML cycle, exactly the trick xterm elements and the .eh-bg background already use. The chat becomes the default view for new sessions; every chat session can pop its raw terminal at any time.
architecture: TARGET (Track B) flow, user keystroke → rendered card: (1) Composer in new module src/chat/composer.ts (multiline textarea, `/` command popup, `@`-file pills, Ctrl+Enter submit, ArrowUp history fed by list_prompt_history) calls chatSend(sessionKey, parts). (2) chatSend goes through the existing invoke() facade in src/platform.ts — desktop: Tauri command `chat_send`; remote: new `case "chat_send"` mapping to POST /api/chat/:threadId/send in src-tauri/src/server.rs. (3) New Rust module src-tauri/src/app_server.rs owns an AppServerManager (managed state registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs beside TerminalManager): one `codex app-server --stdio` child per (account × workspace), spawned with CODEX_HOME/proxy env copied verbatim from terminal.rs::start_terminal's env block; it does initialize/initialized on spawn, then `chat_send` writes a `turn/start` JSON-RPC line. (4) A reader thread (clone of the pty pump in terminal.rs) reads newline-delimited JSON and forwards EVERY notification untyped as one new event `codex-json` {sessionKey, msg} via app.emit — Rust stays a dumb pipe; typing lives in TS generated once by `codex app-server generate-ts` (checked into src/chat/protocol/, pinned to the Codex version). In web mode server.rs re-emits the same frames over a new WS /ws/chat/:id and platform.ts::openChatSocket() re-injects them through the existing emit()/listeners map, so listen("codex-json") is transport-agnostic like pty-data today. (5) src/chat/store.ts — a hand-rolled reducer, no framework — keys a ChatThread per sessionKey and folds notifications: item/started creates a card model; item/agentMessage/delta appends to a text buffer; item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta fills a collapsed thinking block; item/commandExecution/outputDelta appends to a mono output pane; item/completed finalizes; turn/diff/updated feeds a turn-level "Modifications" panel; thread/tokenUsage/updated + account/rateLimits/updated feed header chips; server→client requests (item/commandExecution/requestApproval, item/fileChange/requestApproval, tool/requestUserInput) push blocking approval cards whose buttons resolve the pending JSON-RPC id via `chat_respond`. (6) src/chat/view.ts owns a persistent DOM root per thread (div.chat-shell kept detached in the ChatThread object); render() in src/main.ts never serializes it — a new mountActiveChat(), symmetrical to mountActiveTerminal() (main.ts L4521), re-appends it into the #chatHost slot that render() emits inside section.terminal-shell when the new AppView "chat" is active. Store mutations patch ONLY the affected card node (per-item id → element map), preserving scroll (atBottom heuristic copied from refreshRoom, main.ts L1310) and composer focus. Markdown: bundled marked + DOMPurify inside cards only; everything else keeps the escapeHtml convention. FALLBACK (Track A) flow reuses the same view/store but sources: history via a new `get_discussion_transcript` command in src-tauri/src/discussions.rs (HEAD-fork file via collapse_forks + the contains-then-parse line pattern, returning typed user_message/agent_message events), and live input via the existing sendLine() → write_terminal path with 2s HEAD-file tail refresh. CSS: one new "CHAT LAYER" appended AFTER the Event Horizon block (style.css line 3745+, cascade-order sensitive) consuming only existing tokens (--panel --line --text --muted --accent --accent-ink --radius --eh-glow --font-head/body/mono).
phases: PHASE 1 — Chat shell + read-only transcripts (the UX skeleton, minimal backend). Files: NEW src/chat/{view.ts,store.ts,cards.ts,markdown.ts}; src/main.ts (add AppView 'chat', #chatHost branch in render(), mountActiveChat(), toolbar toggle in bindUi(), wire boot()); src/style.css (new chat layer after L3745: .chat-shell grid [feed 1fr / composer auto], .chat-feed, .chat-card variants --user/--agent/--reasoning/--tool, .chat-composer, all on existing tokens); src-tauri/src/discussions.rs (NEW command get_discussion_transcript(accountId, sessionId) reusing find_rollout_by_id/collapse_forks/is_synthetic_prompt, returning full user_message+agent_message texts with timestamps — the first code anywhere to deserialize agent_message payloads); src-tauri/src/lib.rs (register command); src-tauri/src/server.rs (GET /api/discussions/:id/transcript); src/platform.ts (remoteInvoke case); package.json (add marked + dompurify, bundled — no CDN, Tauri CSP). Acceptance: clicking any discussion in the Discussions view opens it as a markdown chat transcript with correct fork/HEAD handling; scroll position and composer focus survive a full render() (verified by toggling views); terminal view pixel-identical to today; works in both desktop and remote modes.

PHASE 2 — Live bridge chat over the existing PTY (value now, throwaway-thin by design). Files: src/main.ts (extend TerminalSession with chatThread + 'dialogue|terminal' per-session tab in .terminal-shell; default new sessions to dialogue); src/chat/composer.ts (submit → existing sendLine()/write_terminal with \r, exactly like Skill buttons at main.ts L4689; disabled state while codexSessionId is unclaimed); src/chat/store.ts (2s tail poll of get_discussion_transcript with a since-index cursor, appended as cards; 'en cours…' spinner between user send and next agent_message); src-tauri/src/discussions.rs (add since/offset param to transcript command to avoid full re-reads). Acceptance: type a prompt in the composer → it lands in the running Codex TUI → the assistant's reply appears as a markdown card within ~2–3s of rollout flush; the raw-terminal tab shows the same live session; synthetic banner + <environment_context> messages filtered; no interleaving corruption when the user also types in xterm.

PHASE 3 — app-server engine (the real product). Files: NEW src-tauri/src/app_server.rs (AppServerManager: spawn/initialize/reader-pump per account×workspace, commands chat_start_thread, chat_resume_thread(rolloutId), chat_send, chat_steer, chat_interrupt, chat_respond(requestId, decision), chat_stop; env/proxy/CODEX_HOME setup copied from terminal.rs; emit 'codex-json'; -32001 backoff); src-tauri/src/lib.rs (state + 8 command registrations); src/chat/protocol/ (checked-in `codex app-server generate-ts` output, version-pinned); src/chat/store.ts (full notification reducer: item lifecycle, agentMessage/reasoning/commandExecution deltas, fileChange diff cards, mcpToolCall/webSearch/plan cards, turn/diff/updated 'Modifications' panel, unknown-method tolerance); src/chat/cards.ts (renderers per item type incl. stacked diff view); src/main.ts (new-session flow: dialogue sessions create app-server threads, resume maps DiscussionSummary.rolloutId → thread/resume; persist thread ids in the open-terminals localStorage record). Acceptance: a new dialogue session streams assistant tokens live (<100ms cadence); a command execution renders as a card with streaming output and exit code; a file edit renders a diff card; interrupt button stops the turn; app restart resumes the thread with full history; Phase-2 tail-polling disabled for app-server threads.

PHASE 4 — Approvals, steering, and safety UX. Files: src/chat/cards.ts (approvalCard for item/commandExecution/requestApproval + item/fileChange/requestApproval with accept/acceptForSession/decline/cancel; question card for tool/requestUserInput; inline diff preview in file-change approvals); src/chat/composer.ts (Queue-vs-Steer toggle while a turn runs → chat_steer, CodexMonitor pattern); src-tauri/src/app_server.rs (chat_respond plumbs decisions back on the pending JSON-RPC id; serverRequest/resolved clears cards); src-tauri/src/settings.rs + terminal.rs (make ensure_codex_bypass_config MODE-DEPENDENT: never write approval_policy=never/danger-full-access into a CODEX_HOME being used by chat threads unless the account's bypass flag is explicitly on — surfaced as a per-session 'Mode YOLO' chip in the chat header); src/main.ts (desktop notification when an approval/question arrives on a background session; unread badges on sidebar items). Acceptance: with bypass off, an agent file edit blocks on a diff approval card and the decision is honored; with bypass on, the chip is visible and no approval cards appear; steering mid-turn injects without killing the turn.

PHASE 5 — Web/remote parity. Files: src-tauri/src/server.rs (POST /api/chat/threads, /api/chat/:id/send|steer|interrupt|respond, WS /ws/chat/:id?token= streaming raw notification frames, with the same parked-broadcast replay-on-reconnect trick as /ws/terminals — but sized larger and with an explicit resume cursor since Lagged drops that are tolerable for ANSI would corrupt a reduced store); src/platform.ts (remoteInvoke cases for all chat_* commands, openChatSocket() with RECONNECT + since-cursor backfill — fixing the no-reconnect gap terminals live with, then emit('codex-json')). Acceptance: every Phase 3/4 acceptance test passes identically in browser/remote mode against cst-server, including reconnect after killing the WS mid-stream with zero lost or duplicated cards; desktop-only features (launch_ide) stay gated on isRemoteMode() like today.

PHASE 6 — Composer & chrome polish (the OpenCode feel). Files: src/chat/composer.ts (slash-command popup: /nouveau, /modeles via model/list, /compacter → thread/compact/start, /terminal → toggle raw pane, /export transcript, /details tool-verbosity toggle; @-file autocomplete backed by existing list_dir command rendered as pills; prompt history via ArrowUp from list_prompt_history; draft-per-session stash in localStorage); src/chat/view.ts (header chips: model, context % from thread/tokenUsage/updated, rate-limit meter from account/rateLimits/updated reusing the Limits view's data shapes); src/main.ts (sidebar unification: one list mixing live dialogue sessions and resumable discussions with running/unread badges, replacing the separate Discussions entry point; French copy throughout); src/style.css (chips, pills, popup, badges — all in the chat layer). Acceptance: /modeles switches model for the next turn; @-pill inserts a real file reference Codex resolves; token chip visibly climbs during a turn; a first-time user can complete a full edit-approve-iterate loop without ever seeing the raw terminal.
keepsRawTerminal: The terminal is demoted, never removed — three guarantees. (1) Per-session toggle: section.terminal-shell hosts a two-tab strip 'Dialogue | Terminal' per session; for Phase-2 bridge sessions both tabs are literally the same PTY (chat is a lens over it); for Phase-3 app-server sessions the Terminal tab lazily spawns a companion PTY via the untouched start_terminal in the same cwd/CODEX_HOME (for git, builds, debugging), reusing mountActiveTerminal() unchanged. (2) Legacy mode intact: the existing 'Nouveau terminal' modal keeps creating pure PTY sessions with zero chat attached; every current view (pool, limits, dashboard, room, audit, kombai, history) is untouched; AppView just gains one variant. (3) Kill switch: a settings flag (AppSettings, default on) can make 'terminal' the default session type again, so a broken app-server after a Codex CLI upgrade degrades to today's app rather than a dead one — the chat store's unknown-notification tolerance plus this flag is the version-drift insurance.
risks: codex app-server API is version-pinned and partly experimental: generated TS types must be regenerated per Codex CLI upgrade, and notification vocabulary can shift — mitigated by staying on the stable API (no experimentalApi capability), ignoring unknown methods in the reducer, and the terminal-default kill switch; still the single biggest external dependency.

Two engines, one identity: Phase-2 bridge sessions (PTY + rollout tail) and Phase-3 threads (app-server) must map to the same DiscussionSummary/rolloutId identity or the sidebar shows ghost duplicates; the claim_session_for_terminal raciness (up to ~28s, heuristic filename matching) is inherited by bridge mode and only truly fixed by app-server thread ids.

render()'s full innerHTML rebuild is a standing landmine: any contributor who serializes the chat root into a template string (instead of the detached-mount pattern) silently destroys streaming state, focus, and scroll — needs a loud code comment plus the mountActiveChat symmetry to make the pattern obvious.

Approval UX vs bypass-by-default: config.toml already has approval_policy=never/danger-full-access baked in for existing accounts (default bypass=true); Phase 4's mode-dependent bypass touches the hand-rolled TOML lexer and shared per-account config also mutated by agent_room provisioning — concurrent edits and stale bypass keys could make approvals silently never fire, giving false safety.

Markdown introduces the first non-escapeHtml HTML sink in the app: DOMPurify must wrap every marked output, and rollout/agent text can embed hostile HTML/links; CSP review needed for both Tauri webview and cst-server-hosted web mode.

Web parity is a real second implementation (routes + WS + replay + reconnect cursor in server.rs, ~1/3 of Phase 3+4 effort); the existing single-parked-receiver replay design loses frames under Lagged — acceptable for ANSI, fatal for a reduced store — so the chat WS needs its own cursor-based backfill, easy to under-scope.

main.ts is already 4,889 lines with ~40 mutable globals and the feat/agent-room branch has uncommitted changes across 8 of the files this design touches; without landing/rebasing that branch first and enforcing the new src/chat/ module boundary, merge conflicts and regressions are near-certain.

Bridge mode (Phase 2) latency and fidelity are inherently mediocre (rollout flush lag, no tool cards, no streaming) — risk that users judge the chat by Phase 2; messaging and a visible 'mode passerelle' indicator matter, and Phase 2 should be explicitly framed as disposable scaffolding.
effortEstimate: Roughly 19–28 focused dev-days for one senior dev familiar with the repo: Phase 1 ≈ 3–4d (shell, CSS layer, transcript command, dual-mode); Phase 2 ≈ 2–3d (bridge send + tail); Phase 3 ≈ 6–8d (app_server.rs pump, reducer, card renderers, resume); Phase 4 ≈ 3–4d (approvals, steer, mode-dependent bypass); Phase 5 ≈ 3–5d (server.rs routes/WS with reconnect cursor, platform.ts); Phase 6 ≈ 2–4d (composer polish, chips, sidebar unification). First user-visible value (readable transcripts as chat) after ~4 days; the OpenCode-class experience (streaming + tool cards + approvals) after ~15–19 days; web parity and polish complete the tail. Add ~2d contingency for Codex CLI version quirks in app-server and for rebasing onto the landed feat/agent-room branch.
